scope: Theorem 1 of the manuscript “A Fixed Particle Test for Computation in a Forced Viscous Flow” (preprints/A-Fixed-Particle-Test-for-Computation-in-a-Forced-Viscous-Flow-September-27-2026/manuscript.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 376 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 87defbd4577b4c8e), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 3. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: There is an algorithm taking a deterministic single-tape machine M and a finite word w to an effective smooth mean-zero force fM,w for (1), with the following properties. 1. The equation has a global smooth solution uM,w, unique among classical solutions on every finite time interval. 2. For every time order h ≥ 0 and spatial multi-index µ, both t 7−→ ∥∂h t ∂µ XuM,w(t)∥∞, t 7−→ ∥∂h t ∂µ XfM,w(t)∥∞ belong to L∞(0, ∞) ∩ L2(0, ∞). 3. The particle initially at a∗ = (1/8, 3/8, 0) enters O = {(x, y, z) ∈ T3 : 1/2 < x < 1} at a finite time if and only if M halts on w. The force may additionally be chosen divergence free, with unchanged velocity and observation. Constants in the derivative estimates may depend on M, w, ν and the derivative orders. After a loading interval, the prescribed velocity mechanism depends on M but not on w.
